flag_description: Severe or heavy vaginal bleeding reported — possible placenta previa, abruption, or postpartum haemorrhage. Immediate emergency referral required.
recommended_asha_action: Do NOT attempt home management. Call 108 immediately. Keep patient lying flat, do not give anything by mouth, monitor pulse. Accompany patient to nearest FRU/hospital.
source: WHO Recommendations on Antenatal Care for a Positive Pregnancy Experience (2016)

flag_description: Sudden or severe visual disturbance reported — high-risk pre-eclampsia/eclampsia warning sign. Requires immediate BP check and emergency referral.
recommended_asha_action: Measure blood pressure immediately. If BP ≥ 140/90 mmHg, call 108 and arrange urgent transfer to PHC/FRU. Do not leave patient alone.
source: WHO Recommendations on Antenatal Care for a Positive Pregnancy Experience (2016), Section on Hypertensive Disorders

flag_description: Breathing difficulty or acute breathlessness reported during pregnancy — may indicate pulmonary oedema, anaemia, or cardiac complication. Emergency evaluation required.
recommended_asha_action: Sit patient upright. Call 108 immediately. Do not delay — severe breathlessness in pregnancy is a medical emergency.
source: WHO Recommendations on Antenatal Care for a Positive Pregnancy Experience (2016)

flag_description: Severe or unbearable abdominal pain reported — may indicate placental abruption, uterine rupture, or HELLP syndrome. Requires emergency evaluation.
recommended_asha_action: Do not give painkillers. Call 108 immediately. Note onset time and location of pain. Keep patient still and calm. Arrange emergency transport to FRU.
source: WHO Recommendations on Antenatal Care for a Positive Pregnancy Experience (2016)

flag_description: Convulsions or seizures reported — eclampsia is life-threatening for both mother and baby. Highest-priority obstetric emergency.
recommended_asha_action: Call 108 IMMEDIATELY. Place patient on left side to prevent aspiration. Clear airway. Do NOT restrain limbs. Record duration and onset of seizure. Rush to nearest FRU with Magnesium Sulphate capability.
source: WHO Recommendations for Prevention and Treatment of Pre-Eclampsia and Eclampsia (2011)
